title: Sequenced deprecation playbook with pin warnings and migration assistant
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Provide an operationally safe, customer-friendly sequenced deprecation workflow for older model versions that: 1) reduces surprise breaks for production customers, 2) gives clear, actionable migration paths (including automatic pin warnings and a migration assistant), 3) preserves SLOs during rollouts, and 4) emits telemetry to measure migration success and false positives.

Scope: Applies to model versions published in the Redwood catalog that are being retired due to security, performance regressions, cost, or upstream incompatibility. Excludes emergency security takedowns (handled by incident runbooks). Covers hosted API notices, SDK warnings, Console flagged pins, automated migration suggestions, and a 30/14/7/0 notice cadence.

Key components (high level):
- Notice segmentation: automatic audience segmentation by recent usage (30/90/365d), pinned vs unpinned, dedicated/private customers, and contract tier. Notices vary by template and channel (email, Console banner, API warning header, SDK runtime warning).
- Pin-compatibility window: when a version is scheduled for deprecation we offer a configurable compatibility window (default 90 days) during which pinned customers keep the version but receive usage-cost telemetry and recommended alternatives.
- Migration Assistant: a Console + API assistant that: (a) runs model compatibility checks on a customer's pinned routes, (b) suggests target model variants with estimated delta on latency/cost/quality using prior perf profiles, (c) generates a migration checklist and a pre-filled PR for SDK changes where applicable.
- Rollback & fallback policy: automatic fallback to compatible runtime-stable variant (e.g., same architecture but newer weights) for 14 days after cutover if error or quality regression spike detected.
- Telemetry & signals: migration rate, pin retention, error-rate delta, quality regression alerts (via eval sets), customer satisfaction signals (support tickets), and rollback triggers.
- Messaging & legal: standardized notice templates, escalation paths for enterprise customers, and a documented grace/extension request process.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Console shows deprecation banner and link to Migration Assistant for all affected customers within 48 hours of schedule publish.
- SDKs emit a non-blocking runtime warning when calling deprecated versions, including a link to Migration Assistant.
- Migration Assistant produces a recommended target for >= 80% of pinned routes using available perf profiles and compatibility heuristics.
- Telemetry dashboards created for weekly migration metrics and rollback events.
- Playbook documented in Confluence and linked from Console help.

Proposed cadence (example):
- T-90 days: Public deprecation draft published to docs + internal review + enterprise outreach begins. Console shows informational banner for active users.
- T-60 days: Targeted email to owners of pinned routes and high-usage clients with migration checklist link.
- T-30 days: SDK warnings enabled (opt-out for enterprise for contractual reasons). Migration Assistant public.
- T-7 days: Final reminder and recommended force-pin-cutoff date.
- T-0: Version removed from default catalog routing; pinned customers within compatibility window continue to receive support for N days; removal from dedicated pools scheduled per contract.

Risks and mitigations: 
- Risk: Breaking high-volume production customers who cannot migrate in time. Mitigation: default compatibility window, enterprise escalation queue, and temporary extended pin support by Sales/CS.
- Risk: Inaccurate migration recommendations. Mitigation: flag low-confidence suggestions in Migration Assistant and require manual validation; run A/B on a subset.
- Risk: Missed telemetry signals. Mitigation: create synthetic canaries per model variant and surface regression alerts to on-call and CS.

Implementation notes and engineering asks: 
- Console: new Migration Assistant UI flow + banner components + per-route compatibility card. (Depends on ENG-29540 for route metadata expansion.)
- API/SDK: add deprecation header + runtime warning + opt-out header for enterprise.
- Runtime: tagging deprecated versions in catalog and providing inference cost/latency delta estimates (runtime change tracked in runtime-1.22).
- Telemetry: dashboard + automatic alert rules (error-rate > 2x baseline or eval-quality drop > threshold).

Customer communication artifacts: 
- Notice templates: (1) Informational (T-90), (2) Migration recommended (T-60), (3) Final warning (T-7), (4) Post-removal escalation.
- Migration checklist: step-by-step guide (Console, SDK, rollouts, canary tests).

Links and artifacts: 
- Confluence draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RND/PM-42109+Sequenced+Deprecation+Playbook
- Console mockups (Figma): https://www.figma.com/file/xxxxx/deprecation-migration-assistant
- Draft email templates: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/dep-notice-templates
- Related PR (runtime tagging): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1483

Operational runbook snippets: 
- On-call checklist when a deprecation rollback is triggered: run compatibility revert -> notify CS -> open emergency pin extension ticket.
- Postmortem triggers: customer-visible outage or >10% pinned-route failures.

Success metrics (90 days after cutover): 
- >= 60% of affected non-enterprise routes migrated to recommended variants without manual CS intervention.
- <1% of deprecations escalate to urgent enterprise extensions.
- Migration Assistant recommended target accepted rate >= 50% when confidence high.
